requirements.requirement: curl is pinned/held at its currently installed version so it will not be upgraded
requirements.summary: Executor captured curl-8.17.0-r1 as the installed version, then ran `apk add curl=8.17.0-r1` which wrote an exact version constraint into /etc/apk/world (verified via grep showing `curl=8.17.0-r1`). This is the correct apk-tools v3 mechanism for pinning since --no-upgrade is not supported in this version.

requirements.requirement: A system update does not upgrade curl while other packages update normally
requirements.summary: A simulated upgrade (cmd-2b6156ff148d4450) showed curl excluded from 58 scheduled package upgrades. A real `apk upgrade` was then executed (cmd-f4ce387e5bbc43f3), upgrading 56 packages (kernel, musl, openssl, util-linux, etc.) while curl remained at 8.17.0-r1, the world pin stayed intact, and curl remained functional post-upgrade.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 with full pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 1d261123-9739-4626-8663-4e36249d15dc with curl healthy and pin intact (cmd-f3d98fa2c03349f1). Reboot was issued via backgrounded sudo command with the exec stream closing on disconnect, consistent with a reboot in progress (cmd-178902305e6144e8). After a polling period the node came back with a different boot_id ea6e5d0a-0adc-481b-a680-c79f779fcb7b (cmd-0dcc4b1e33204aa9), matching the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot. Post-restart state confirmed curl still at 8.17.0-r1, world pin intact, curl functional, and kernel upgraded to 6.18.54-0-lts with fresh uptime, confirming both the update and reboot took full effect while curl was held (cmd-5137ed12e9714182). This is corroborated by the independent fixed lifecycle boot-identity cross-check (before_prepare -> after_executor).

overall_summary: The executor correctly pinned curl to its installed version 8.17.0-r1 by writing an exact version constraint into /etc/apk/world (the correct mechanism for apk-tools v3, which lacks --no-upgrade), then validated the pin held during both a simulated and a real system upgrade that touched 56 other packages. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was fully and coherently demonstrated: healthy pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot identity matching the fixed lifecycle snapshot, and recovered state showing curl still pinned and functional after the upgrade and reboot. Minor hygiene deduction for two leftover temporary log files.
limitations: The restart acknowledgement (cmd-178902305e6144e8) is inferred from the exec stream closing rather than an explicit success message from the reboot command itself, though this is consistent with expected behavior when a node reboots mid-connection.
Connection-timeout commands during the reboot window (e.g., cmd-27f8ab49659c478c, cmd-b0e9293663d34533) are expected transient failures during the disruption and were not treated as task failures.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command timeline reviewed chronologically. cmd-2e78b43630f649ee was read-only baseline capture. cmd-8e5a89ade1634deb attempted `apk update` plus `apk add --no-upgrade` which failed (unrecognized option); the `apk update` refreshed the repo index cache, a low-risk, non-destructive side effect directly needed to discover the correct pinning syntax, and is a reasonable corrective/discovery step rather than an unnecessary mutation. cmd-78144ff9854341cb and cmd-904a4266c7244b9b were pure read-only `--help` discovery commands with no state change. The real `apk upgrade` (cmd-f4ce387e5bbc43f3) is a broad system mutation (56 packages incl. kernel) but is directly tied to verifying the material task outcome (that a real update leaves curl untouched) and to the mandatory restart protocol, so it has a clear causal role rather than being an unnecessary mutation. The reboot (cmd-178902305e6144e8) is required by the fixed restart-evidence protocol. One minor hygiene issue: two temporary log files (/tmp/reboot.log and /tmp/upgrade_sim.log) were created and left behind, visible as residue in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot; they were not cleaned up, though they are small, non-sensitive, and low-risk.
